question: T and U start a business. T invests ₹40,000. After 3 months, U joins with ₹60,000. After 3 more months, T doubles his capital. If the business runs for 12 months, find the profit ratio of T to U.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit ∝ Capital × Time

T: 40000×3 + 40000×3 + 80000×6 = 120000 + 120000 + 480000 = 720000

U: 60000×9 = 540000

Ratio = 720000 : 540000

**∴ Answer = 4 : 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

T invests ₹40000 initially

After 3 months, U invests ₹60000

After next 3 months, T doubles capital to ₹80000

Total time = 12 months

**Formula used:**

Profit ∝ Capital × Time

 T: 40k (0-3) T: 40k (3-6) T: 80k (6-12) U: 60k (3-12) 

**Calculations:**

⇒ T: 40000×3 = 120000

⇒ T: 40000×3 = 120000

⇒ T: 80000×6 = 480000

⇒ Total T = 720000

⇒ U: 60000×9 = 540000

⇒ Ratio = 720000 : 540000

⇒ Divide by 180000 ⇒ 4 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Capital-Time Rule

Profit share = Capital × Time. Always break into intervals when capital changes.

Joining Midway

If a partner joins later, calculate time from joining to end.

Changing Capital

When capital changes, treat each period separately.

Ratio Simplification

Divide both terms by highest common factor to get simplest ratio.

38:T
